rationale: The SEMICOLON guard on a parameter-entity reference, which no committed fixture pinned before this one. `xml/xsd-parameter-entity-refs` pins the OTHER guard — it forbids a `references` edge to `zz` for the value form `% zz '<'`, so a rule accepting any `%...;` would be caught there. The semicolon test had no pin, and it is precisely the guard that deleting the analyzer's last regular expression put at risk. `grammars/tree-sitter-xml/xml/src/grammar.json` defines `PEReference = SEQ[STRING "%", SYMBOL Name, STRING ";"]`, so a well-formed node always ends in `;` — but `<!ELEMENT %unterminated EMPTY>`, a reference missing its semicolon, still yields a `PEReference` node whose only named child is a `Name` and whose text is `%unterminated` with no `;` in it. Re-probed through production `parseFile`: the shipped predicate publishes 3 relationships and NO edge for that node, while a `Name`-child lookup publishes a fourth (`references root -> unterminated`) for a document that never wrote `%unterminated;`. Authored from that re-probe rather than before it, and the value it pins was confirmed by `validation/m14/fixtures/xml/pereference-shape-probe.mts` on 11 obtainable `PEReference` nodes (4 fixture, 7 synthetic, 0 corpus — see its `corpus.counts` for why the corpus supplies none). The four rows: (0/0b) `declared` and `unterminated` are declared so row 1 can RESOLVE and row 2 cannot be satisfied by refusing undeclared names; (1) `%declared;` in the internal subset is PUBLISHED, owned by the DOCTYPE; (2) `<!ELEMENT %unterminated EMPTY>` is NOT published; (3) `% zz '<`, the parameter-entity VALUE form, is a DECLARATION of `zz` and not a use, so NOT published. The two references use different names on purpose: edge identity here is source|type|target, so one name would collapse the defect into the existing edge and the forbid row could not see it.

expectRelationships.note: The positive row. `%declared;` is a direct child of the internal subset, so the owner is the DOCTYPE's own name — there is no element above it. `resolvable: in-document` because row 0 declares `declared`, which is what stops the forbid rows below from being satisfied by a rule that publishes nothing at all.
Row 0b. `unterminated` IS declared, so row 2's forbid cannot be met by refusing undeclared names — it can only be met by the semicolon guard itself.

forbidRelationships.note: THE ROW THIS FIXTURE EXISTS FOR. `<!ELEMENT %unterminated EMPTY>` is the parameter-entity reference form with its semicolon MISSING. The grammar still builds a `PEReference` node for it, with a `Name` child and no `;` in its text, so reading the child publishes a use of a name the document never wrote `%unterminated;`. Inventing that edge is the fabrication rule's exact case: it would be counted unexplained and would poison bb_graph and bb_impact. Mutant xml/pereference-semicolon-guard-removed reinstates the defect and must fail this row.

The parameter-entity VALUE form `% zz '<` names nothing: it DECLARES `zz` and its replacement text, it does not use `zz`. Repeated here in the bare internal-subset position because it is a different parse shape from xml/xsd-parameter-entity-refs — children `ERROR,Name,ERROR` rather than a clean `Name` — and the probe measured the two shapes reaching the same guard by different routes.
direction: the DOCTYPE's own name owns both references. Nothing in this document makes a parameter entity use another.

forbidSymbols.name: zz
forbidSymbols.note: the value form's first token is not a parameter entity name, so nothing may be published for it — the same refusal xml/xsd-parameter-entity-refs pins for the replacement-text position.
